newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CM Telecom sees continued good growth.
newsitem.headline: CM Telecom sees continued good growth.

text.p: Telecommunications equipment and service provider CM Telecom International Ltd expects to sustain double digit earnings growth despite keen competition in China, its major market, company officials said on Thursday.

"The telecommunications industry is still a growth market and we are diversifying into other related areas. We believe we can sustain our growth," chairman and managing director Tony Hau told Reuters.

"Despite the keen competition, we have managed to increase our local and roaming subscriber base during the year. Our margins have been affected, but we are taking definite steps towards reducing our costs," he added.
China accounted for over 85 percent of the group's turnover of HK$886.95 million for year ended March 31, 1997.
Hua was speaking after the company reported net profit in fiscal year 1996 grew 12 percent to HK$90.17 million.
The better performance was attributed to strong growth in its paging, maintenance and leasing operations, said executive director Frank Wu.
Together the three operations accounted for 51 percent of the group's pre-tax profit.
CM Telecom continues to invests in trunk radio systems, microwave radio systems and China Nationwide paging system and plans to make more investments Hong Kong and China.
"We are looking into providing higher margin products in order to have healthier earnings growth," Wu said.
This included supplying systems software and other after sales support systems, Hau said.
CM Telecom holds one of the 20 government licences to set up a China-wide paging network.

Together with Shenzhen-based China Motion Telecom Development Company (CMTDC) and the Guangdong Mobile communications Corporation, it has a contract to supply the first trunked radio system to cross the Hong Kong-China border.
